newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TO CUT IMPORT SURCHARGE BY 2PCT ON MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TO CUT IMPORT SURCHARGE BY 2PCT ON MONDAY.

text.p: Hungary will cut the surcharge on all imported goods from six to four percent from Monday but said it had not yet set a date for the next decrease.
The Finance Ministry told Hungarian news agency MTI on Friday there had been no decision yet on the pace of decreasing the remaining 4 percent.

The government first introduced an eight percent import surcharge in March 1995 as part of its austerity programme which succeeded in reining in the country's soaring current account and trade deficits.

Last year it announced it would honour its international obligations to phase out the tax completely by July 1 1997. It introduced two one-percentage-point cuts in 1996 and said it planned three reductions of two points each in 1997, on January 1, April 1 and June 30. However, the January cut was postponed.

Finance Ministry experts say the tariff has proven successful by raising central budget revenues by 68 billion forints in 1995 and by 99 billion forints in 1996, and increasing domestic producers' competitiveness within the country.
